text: The business problem and the stack are settled. Now the feature list: what actually goes into the churn model, pulled from five real tables in EVERPEAK_PROD.
Three families -- account and plan details from Accounts and Subscriptions, usage behavior from UsageEvents, and support and billing signals from SupportTickets and Invoices.
The rule behind every single one: a feature only counts if we'd genuinely know it on the actual day we're predicting -- not something only knowable in hindsight.
Logins in the last 30 and 90 days, days since last login, open tickets, days late on the last invoice -- each one windowed back from a reference point for that account.
The feature spec is signed off with Renata. Next: how we'll actually judge whether this model, once trained, is good enough to act on.
